ap23: root-cause analysis of the missing `move $v0,$a0` (110 under sn-n64-281 -mfp32; 210 default). Dumped cc1n64 (-ds/-dc) for every variant. In cse the copy B=A (vol = quotient) is only kept when B (the user var) is the canonical reg of the quantity: make_regs_eqv (cse.c) promotes NEW only when its last use is beyond the cse extended block (or its first uid is before the block start) and later than the old first reg; otherwise every use is rewritten to the div result A and the copy is deleted. Making vol canonical (vol also set in the else arm: `vol = o->unk70 * 100; o->unk64 = vol;`, or `vol = 0;` at the top) with the store written BEFORE the copy (`o->vol = q; vol = o->vol;`) gives cse the exact shape (store uses A, compare uses B, `move 87,162`), BUT combine.c then folds `B = A` into the single use `slt` (LOG_LINK, B dies there), so the final asm still has no move: all of those score 110 (fp32) / 210. If both store and compare use B, combine instead folds the copy into the div (div -> B directly). So the target needs B to survive combine: either B has >=2 live uses (the store uses A after combine substitution, slt keeps B) or a basic-block boundary between the copy and the slt that jump2 removes later; neither source shape found. First quotient must NOT share the variable (vol also for the first quotient: 945/640). Tried (all no effect or worse): readback `vol = o->vol` (110), compare o->vol (110), identical-arm if (cse merges it, 110), vol=0 initial (110), else-arm vol reuse (945 with shared first quotient, 110 separate). See also earlier notes.

Reading cc1n64 -dl/-dS: pseudos 90 (b2, life 6 insns) / 91 (a2, life 4) / 92 (dz): local-alloc ranks by refs/life, so the shorter-lived a2 should take f0 first (as in the x/y groups). In ours it does not: b2/dz got f0 and a2 f2, which is what happens when a2 is loaded BEFORE b2 (final asm: `lwc1 f2,0x18; lwc1 f0,0x28`), while the target loads b2 first (`lwc1 f2,0x28; lwc1 f0,0x18`). sched1 itself orders them b2 (insn 37) then a2 (39) (`insn 39 has a greater potential hazard, now 39 37`), so the swap is made later (sched2 or the priority at allocation); the z group is the last group in the block (z difference written first in the source). So the open lever is the load order/lives of the z pair at allocation time, not the sqrt or stores. Nothing new compiled; saved best 747 default / 334 -mfp32, profile not applied (not exact).

Not libultra, libgcc or libmus: it is the game's own cartridge-bus device driver around the PI helpers func_8000ABE8 (wait PI_STATUS, store), func_8000AC20 (wait, load) and func_8000AC5C (delay loop of 0x3E8 spins): it writes a command word and two arguments to 0xB1FFFFE4/E8/EC/E0 (cart domain 1 registers), then polls 0xB1FFFFF0 and 0xB1FFFFE0 until the device answers, and reads 0xB1FFFFDC. No ultralib or libgcc routine reads or writes those addresses, so no SDK digest or reference source applies. Why it is assembly: the body holds a literal `break 1` in the middle of the retry loop (after clearing 0xB1FFFFE0, before re-sending the command), which no compiler emits from C (GCC only writes break 7 and break 6 for divides); the judge refuses the inline asm that would make it, and the m2c draft's M2C_BREAK(1) scores 640 with no C spelling of it. The jr ra; nop epilogue and unfilled slots match the KMC 2.7.2 style of the neighbouring PI helpers, so the surrounding library is compiled C, but this routine's `break 1` is hand-written. Seven callers (func_8000B6F0, func_8000B73C, func_8000B7CC, func_8000B85C, ...) read its result. Set aside as assembly; a human who knows the device may name it.
